# song2mv

> Song in, beat-synced lyric timing (LRC, SRT, word-timed JSON) and a code-drawn music video out. A command-line
> tool built for coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Alpha (0.x): formats may change; every JSON output
> carries schema_version.

Install (not on PyPI yet): `uv tool install --python 3.13 "song2mv[sync] @ git+https://github.com/yongjip/song2mv"`
(needs ffmpeg; `render` also needs Node 18+; the sync extra needs Python ≤ 3.14).

## Commands

- `song2mv sync AUDIO [--lyrics FILE] --language CODE [--title TEXT] [--json]` — beat grid, word-timed lyrics, song.lrc,
  song.words.lrc, song.srt, mv.json and music.json (loudness, section boundaries) in a work folder. Takes minutes (several whisper runs); run it in the
  background. The --json result lists `outputs` and `check_by_ear` (lines to verify by ear).
- `song2mv beats AUDIO [--bpm auto|N] [--json]` — tempo and beat grid only.
- `song2mv click WORK --from A --to B [--words] [--json]` — a wav of that stretch with clicks on the beat grid and
  ticks on lyric words, for a person to listen to (an agent cannot hear the song); the result says what to ask.
- `song2mv check VIDEO --song mv.json [--from A --to B] [--json]` — experimental; per-line motion, coverage,
  chorus variation, cut rhythm. Passing is necessary, not proof of fun.
- `song2mv sheet VIDEO [--song mv.json] (--every S | --times T,T | --lines ID,ID | --cuts CHECK_JSON) [--from A]
  [--crop X,Y,W,H] [--json]` — a PNG contact sheet of a rendered video, captions included: frames at song times, each
  labelled with its time and the line sung; `--lines` takes one in the last word of each line named, `--cuts` one
  from each shot listed in a saved `check --json` result.
- `song2mv render mv.json [--from A --to B] [--aspect 16x9|9x16|both] [--still T] [--template DIR] [--json]` —
  experimental; uses Remotion, which is not MIT: free for individuals and companies with up to 3 employees, a
  company license otherwise.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 `check` found a failing check, 2 error. With --json an error is
`{"ok": false, "error": {"message", "kind", "hint"}}` on stdout; do what the hint says.
